C031.metal: .925 sterling silver · 1.41 g · 16 mm · plain · circulated / toned · white 2×2 staple flip

C031.label: Australia · 1943 · Threepence (3d)
C031.notes: SER OC-AU-001. George VI · IND:IMP still in legend (Emperor of India — pre-1948 drop). Reverse: three wheat stalks · AUSTRALIA · THREE PENCE · 1943 · S. Country #10. Wartime: Australia needed silver change, US mints helped. Pocket money from a Pacific-war economy — melt, not face. Junk Ag = melt (see SILVER.md). SER siblings: OC-AU-002 (1944 Perth penny) · OC-AU-003 (1966 platypus 20¢). Australia flips now 3.
C031.story: A 1943 Australian threepence, struck in the middle of World War II. King George VI is on the front, and the back shows three stalks of wheat by George Kruger Gray, a design used since 1938 — before the war began. It's made of real silver, which is why it feels different from today's coins in your hand.

C249.metal: cupronickel · 11.30 g · 28.52 mm · reeded · circulated · white 2×2 staple flip
C249.specs: thickness unknown · medal alignment · first-year decimal
C249.design: obverse Elizabeth II · reverse Stuart Devlin platypus in water · big 20
C249.label: Australia · 1966 · 20 Cents
C249.notes: SER OC-AU-003. Photo confirmed · user shorthand 1966. Reverse Stuart Devlin platypus in water · big 20 (Queen / date obverse not shown — Joseph dated 1966). First calendar year of Australian decimal currency (C-Day 14 Feb 1966) — the platypus replaced florin-weight change in tills overnight. Shop / tram / pub twenty-cent piece while your wartime pre-decimal C031 / OC-AU-001 (1943-S 3d) and C239 / OC-AU-002 (1944 Perth penny) were already history. Third Australia flip; Kangaroos remain B013/B016. Australia flips now 3.
